title: bug: a failed LogRotator compression can leave activity.log.rotating.tmp behind, because compressFile rejects right after destination.destroy() without waiting for the write stream to close, so rotate()'s cleanup rmSync can run before the stream's async open creates the file; LogRotator.rotateFailure.test.ts (f2) flakes under full-suite load
description:
Reported by qa-25f21f0a (msg-a7f361af, 06:05Z on 2026-11-04) while gating task-77e54ebb on tip 3500ae19 in a git-archive snapshot:
- src/util/LogRotator.rotateFailure.test.ts case f2 ("five failing rotations keep everything…") failed once in the full daemon run.
- The failure was an extra `activity.log.rotating.tmp` in the directory listing (expectSeededState, :65).
- f2 passed 3/3 alone, and an immediate full re-run was green (286 files, 7475 tests).
The test came with task-1f84f4e4 (d4a387ef, DONE). Any checkRef that runs the whole daemon suite can hit it.

CAUSE, read at tip 2a1c5a36 (packages/moe-daemon/src/util/LogRotator.ts):
- rotate() (:106-137) awaits compressFile(this.logPath, pendingPath). On a rejection its catch calls fs.rmSync(pendingPath, { force: true }) and rethrows.
- compressFile (:141+) creates the destination with fs.createWriteStream(destPath), whose open() is asynchronous. rejectOnce (:166-184) calls destination.destroy() and then reject() at once, without waiting for the destination's 'close'.
- When the failing gzip errors on its first chunk before the destination's open has completed, rotate()'s rmSync finds nothing to delete. The late open then creates activity.log.rotating.tmp, and the file outlives the failed rotation.
- In production this only leaves a stray tmp until the next rotation's step 1 removes it. In the test it breaks the exact listing assertion whenever the suite is busy.

FIX DIRECTION: in rejectOnce, settle only after the destroyed destination has emitted 'close' (or after its open finished), so rotate()'s cleanup always runs after the file can exist. Keep the timeout and the error passthrough. Do not just loosen the test: the f1/f2 listing assertions are the contract task-1f84f4e4 added. Follow gotcha-activity-log-rotated-generations in Serena memory.
definitionOfDone: A deterministic test fails on today's code. It makes the destination's open complete only after the gzip error, for example by delaying the open or by awaiting destination close in a spy, and shows activity.log.rotating.tmp left behind after a failed rotate(). It passes after the fix, which settles compressFile's rejection only once the destination stream has closed.

LogRotator.rotateFailure.test.ts passes 20 consecutive runs (`npx vitest run src/util/LogRotator.rotateFailure.test.ts --repeat 20` or an equivalent loop), and its f1/f2 directory-listing assertions are unchanged.
npm test and npx tsc --noEmit pass in packages/moe-daemon, run in a snapshot outside the shared checkout.

implementationPlan.description:
Fix packages/moe-daemon/src/util/LogRotator.ts so a failed compression settles only after its destination has closed.
- Export `DESTINATION_CLOSE_WAIT_MS = 5_000` right after ROTATION_RETRY_DELAY_MS, with the doc line 'How long a failed compression waits for its destination to close before rejecting anyway'.
- Error handling in compressFile's rejectOnce: keep settled, clearTimeout(timeout), unpipeStreams() and the three conditional destroy() calls exactly as they are. Replace only the final reject(...) with this:
  - build `failure` with the same normalization (error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)));
  - if destination.closed, reject(failure) at once;
  - otherwise arm `const closeWait = setTimeout(() => reject(failure), DESTINATION_CLOSE_WAIT_MS)`, call closeWait.unref?.(), and add `destination.once('close', () => { clearTimeout(closeWait); reject(failure); })`.
- Add a comment that says why. fs.createWriteStream opens its file asynchronously, and destroy() lets a pending open finish before it closes the fd. Rejecting first let rotate()'s cleanup rmSync run before the late open recreated the temporary file. The bound keeps a hung open from stalling appendActivity forever, since it awaits rotateIfNeeded under the activity mutex.
- Every rejection path goes through this: source error, gzip error, destination error (autoDestroy closes it in the same tick, so no real wait), and the 30 s timeout.
- Unchanged: the success path (resolve on 'finish'), rotate(), rotateIfNeeded, the error passed through, COMPRESSION_TIMEOUT_MS. No new option and no env var.
Then both new cases pass, 9/9 across the two files.
implementationPlan.note: Exported DESTINATION_CLOSE_WAIT_MS = 5_000 after ROTATION_RETRY_DELAY_MS. rejectOnce keeps settled/clearTimeout/unpipe/destroy calls and now rejects at once only if destination.closed, else on the destination's 'close', bounded by an unref'd DESTINATION_CLOSE_WAIT_MS timer cleared on close. Success path, rotate(), rotateIfNeeded untouched. Snapshot run of both LogRotator test files: 9/9 passed (was 2 failed | 7 passed at base).

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A failed or timed-out LogRotator compression rejects only after its destination write stream has closed, bounded by DESTINATION_CLOSE_WAIT_MS (5 s). So rotate()'s cleanup always runs after the temporary file can exist, and a failed rotation never leaves activity.log.rotating.tmp behind, even when the stream's async open lands after the gzip error.
acceptanceCriteria: (f5) A failed rotation whose destination open completes only after the gzip error leaves the directory listing unchanged and no activity.log.rotating.tmp. It fails on today's code.
A destination whose destroy never completes still rejects compressFile, at DESTINATION_CLOSE_WAIT_MS and not before.
LogRotator.rotateFailure.test.ts passes with --repeats 20, and f1-f4 are unchanged.
tsc --noEmit and the full daemon npm test pass in a snapshot.
invariants: compressFile settles exactly once on every path
A failed rotation leaves .1-.N.gz and the live log untouched
No path can hang appendActivity: the close wait is bounded and unref'd
compatibility: No change to the activity-log format, the rotation order (task-1f84f4e4's tmp-first chain), rotateIfNeeded's swallow-and-retry-delay contract, the env vars, or any MCP contract.

completionSummary: LogRotator.compressFile's rejectOnce now settles a failed or timed-out compression only after the destroyed destination stream has closed (immediately if destination.closed), bounded by new export DESTINATION_CLOSE_WAIT_MS = 5000 via an unref'd timer cleared on 'close'. rotate()'s cleanup rmSync therefore always runs after a late async open could have created the file, so a failed rotation no longer leaves activity.log.rotating.tmp (the (f2) full-suite flake). Tests: new (f5) in LogRotator.rotateFailure.test.ts (open gated through the stream fs option, released after the gzip error; fails on base) and a bound case in LogRotator.test.ts (Writable that never closes, fake timers: rejects at exactly 5000 ms, not before). f1-f4 unchanged. RED at base 2 failed | 7 passed; mutants MA (reject immediately) and MB (no bound) both caught. Gate: tsc clean, rotateFailure --repeats 20 passed, full daemon suite 289 files / 7513 passed | 24 skipped, rotator pin ok; qualityGate parity-check + lint pass. Note: the DoD's --repeat is not a vitest 5 flag; --repeats is.
